For the aforementioned AWS Cognito, the SDK provides an API for handling all 
operations such as sign-in and registration. Additionally, the SDK can produce 
access tokens which can be sent within the HTTP header, to later authenticate 
the user on the cloud. 
The data management of the application is centred around the utilisation of the 
cloud services, with minimal data stored on device. Storing data on the cloud 
ensures that session states remain device agnostic, addressing the needs of a 
modern user who may replace or change their phone regularly. 
The AWS SDK, abstracts the management and storage of user sessions, 
ensuring security. When a user signs-in AWS Cognito will generate a session 
token that will be stored in the cloud. This token is critical for maintaining the 
users signed-in state; additionally, the token automatically refreshes, improving 
security (AWS, n.d.). 
Ensuring the accessibility of the application, requires attending to many 
disabilities, including visual, auditory, and cognitive. The use of strong contrast 
ratios, adhering to (WCAG, 2023)’s minimum of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 
for large text. Additionally, text should be scalable and not lose content as the 
text becomes larger, within Android Java, this involves using relative units such 
as sp for font sizes, ensuring text scales dynamically with the mobile's system 
settings. 
With the application potentially expanding into overseas territories, the 
application's architecture must be able to be easily adapted to support various 
languages and regions, without the need for significant changes. This can be 
accomplished by storing all strings, labels, and other region-specific content 
within distinct resource files. Additionally, some elements that are region-
specific, such as reading from left to right, can be easily handled based on
